caption: A cyclist riding along a flat street stops pedalling and rests both feet on the pedals, and the bicycle coasts on down the street, gradually slowing.
expectation: The bicycle keeps rolling forward after the legs stop, with no pause or jolt at the moment pedalling ends; the path stays straight and the wheels keep turning; it slows only gently, never speeding up, stopping dead, or rolling backward while the feet stay still.

caption: A girl spinning on an office chair grabs the edge of the desk to stop, and her ponytail swings on around her head after the chair has stopped.
expectation: The hair continues in the direction of the spin for a moment after the chair halts and then falls; it does not stop with the chair or swing the other way first.

caption: A stack of newspapers rides a conveyor belt in a printing plant, and when the belt is stopped the stack slides on a little before halting.
expectation: The slide is in the belt's former direction and starts as the belt stops; the stack stops within a short distance and does not slide backward.

caption: The cord holding a hanging flowerpot on a porch snaps, and the pot falls and breaks on the boards below.
expectation: The pot drops straight down the moment the cord parts, speeding up, and breaks on impact with soil spilling; it does not hover or fall sideways.

caption: A gymnast hanging from a pair of rings lets go and drops onto the mat below.
expectation: She falls straight down as soon as her hands open, bending her knees on landing; the empty rings swing after she leaves them.

caption: A man leaning over a balcony rail fumbles his phone, and it falls into the swimming pool below with a splash.
expectation: The phone falls straight down, faster as it goes, and enters the water with a splash then sinks; it does not drift outward or float.

caption: A boy running through a shopping mall mistakes a closed glass door for an open one, runs into it, and bounces back onto the floor.
expectation: He stops dead at the glass and is thrown back; the door stays closed and intact; no part of him passes through the pane.

caption: A footballer's shot hits the crossbar and the ball drops down onto the goal line.
expectation: The ball rebounds off the bar at the moment of contact and falls under gravity; the bar does not bend and the ball does not pass through it.

caption: A pool player breaks a tight triangle of balls with the cue ball, and the balls scatter across the table in all directions.
expectation: The balls move only after being struck, spread outward from the impact, and none overlaps another; the cue ball slows sharply.

caption: A boy kicks a ball against a tree trunk, and it bounces back to him.
expectation: The rebound begins at contact and comes back slower than the kick; the tree does not move and the ball does not go into it.

caption: A bottle cap spun on a kitchen counter spins in place, slows, and rattles to a stop.
expectation: The spin slows steadily and the cap wobbles more as it slows; it does not speed up or stop instantly.

caption: A woman squeezes a wet bar of soap in her hand in the bath, and it slips out of her grip and skids across the bottom of the tub.
expectation: The soap leaves the hand as the fingers close on it and shoots out in one direction, not straight up or back into the hand; it skids across the wet surface in a straight line and slows to a stop or stops against the side of the tub; it does not hover, change direction on its own, or stay stuck to the hand.

caption: A man shoves a cardboard box across a smooth garage floor, and it slides out onto the gravel driveway and stops almost at once.
expectation: The box slides freely in a straight line on the smooth floor, and its sharp slowing begins exactly where the gravel starts, not before; it does not glide on across the gravel as it did indoors, stop dead while still on the smooth floor, or speed up; it stays flat on the ground the whole way.

caption: A woman lobs a water balloon over a garden fence to a friend, and it arcs over and lands in the friend's hands.
expectation: The balloon rises, clears the fence at the top of its arc, and falls into the hands, wobbling in flight; it does not travel flat or hang above the fence.

caption: An angler swings a rod and casts a weighted line far out over a lake, and the weight splashes into the water.
expectation: The weight flies in an arc, pulling line behind it, and drops into the water; it does not stop in the air or fly straight.

caption: A boy crumples a page into a ball and tosses it across the office toward a bin, and it drops into the bin.
expectation: The paper ball follows an arc, slowing near its peak, and falls into the bin; it does not float or change direction midway.

caption: A child builds a house of playing cards on a table, and when someone bumps the table the house collapses into a heap.
expectation: The collapse begins at the bump and runs through the structure in under a second; every card ends flat or leaning on the table; none stays balanced in the air.

caption: A toddler stacks sofa cushions into a tower and pushes it, and the tower topples over onto the rug.
expectation: The tower leans away from the push and the top cushions fall first; the cushions land on the side away from the toddler.

caption: A man carrying a long ladder turns around in a yard, and the far end of the ladder knocks over a bin.
expectation: The bin tips at the moment the ladder end hits it and falls in the direction of the swing, spilling; it does not move before contact.

caption: A woman pulls the cord of a window blind, and the blind gathers upward as the cord runs down through her hands.
expectation: The blind rises only as fast as the cord is pulled and stops when she stops; the cord stays taut on the pulled side and does not stretch.

caption: A puppeteer lifts a marionette off the stage by its control bar, and the strings go taut and the puppet's limbs hang from them.
expectation: The strings straighten as the bar lifts, the limbs rise only when their strings tighten, and the strings go slack when the puppet is set down.

caption: A sailor hauls in the anchor rope of a small boat, and the rope comes up taut and dripping until the anchor breaks the surface.
expectation: The rope runs straight down into the water under load and stays taut while pulled; water drips from it; the anchor appears only when enough rope is in.

caption: A yoga student sits on a foam block, and the block compresses under her and springs back when she stands.
expectation: The block flattens only while she sits and recovers its shape within a second or two of her standing; it does not stay squashed.

caption: A child squeezes a rubber duck under the bathwater and lets go, and the duck squirts water and puffs back to shape.
expectation: The duck flattens while squeezed, a jet of water comes out of its hole, and it refills and rounds out when released.

caption: A potter presses a thumb into the side of a soft clay pot on the wheel, and the pot keeps the dent.
expectation: The wall dents inward under the thumb and stays dented after it lifts; the clay does not spring back.

caption: A hairdresser snips a lock of hair with scissors, and the cut hair falls to the floor.
expectation: The lock separates exactly where the blades close and drops straight down; the hair on the head is shorter where it was cut and does not regrow.

caption: A carpenter saws through a plank on a sawhorse, and the cut end drops to the ground as the saw comes through.
expectation: The kerf deepens with each stroke, sawdust falls, and the piece parts only when the saw is through; the two pieces do not rejoin.

caption: An office worker feeds a sheet of paper into a shredder, and it comes out the bottom as a bundle of thin strips.
expectation: The sheet is drawn in at the top and strips emerge below as it passes; the sheet does not reappear whole.

caption: A cook ladles pancake batter onto a hot griddle, and the batter spreads into a round puddle and stops.
expectation: The batter flows outward from where it lands, slows as it spreads, and settles into a round; it does not keep spreading or climb back into the ladle.

caption: A gardener drops a large stone into a bucket full of water, and water spills over the rim onto the ground.
expectation: The splash and overflow happen as the stone enters, the level stays at the rim afterward, and the stone sinks to the bottom; the stone does not pass through the bucket.

caption: A child stomps a foot in a full bathtub, and water sloshes up the sides and splashes over the edge onto the floor.
expectation: The wave rises where the foot lands and travels outward, spilling at the rim; the water settles back level afterwards.

caption: A bucket with a hole near its bottom is filled from a tap, and a thin stream squirts out of the hole and arcs onto the ground.
expectation: The stream comes only from the hole, arcs outward and down, and gets weaker as the level in the bucket falls; it does not squirt upward.

caption: A barista pours coffee beans from a bag into a grinder hopper, and the beans rattle down and fill the hopper in a heap.
expectation: The beans fall in a stream and pile up from the bottom, settling into a rough cone; a few bounce out onto the counter.

caption: A child pours sand through a plastic funnel into a bottle, and sand runs through the neck in a steady stream while a cone builds inside the bottle.
expectation: The stream is thin and steady, the cone grows inside the bottle, and the funnel empties from the bottom; the sand does not stop in the funnel.

caption: A farmer tips a sack of potatoes onto a barn floor, and the potatoes tumble out and roll apart into a loose spread.
expectation: The potatoes fall and roll away from the pile, coming to rest scattered; they do not stack or stay in the sack's shape.

caption: A skydiver pulls the ripcord, and the parachute unfolds and snaps open into a canopy above her.
expectation: The canopy fills with air and rounds out above her, and her fall slows sharply the moment it opens; the lines go taut.

caption: A sailor lets the sail of a small boat loose in a breeze, and the sail fills and bellies out to one side.
expectation: The sail bulges away from the wind and flaps when the wind drops; it does not belly toward the wind.

caption: A gust of wind reaches a row of wind turbines on a hill, and the blades start turning and speed up.
expectation: The blades begin turning only when the wind arrives and slow when it drops; all turbines turn the same way.

caption: A gymnast performs a cartwheel across a mat, hands then feet touching the ground in turn.
expectation: Her hands and feet touch the mat one after another in sequence, her body stays whole and bends only at the joints, and she lands upright.

caption: A window cleaner climbs a ladder rung by rung to reach a second-floor window.
expectation: Hands and feet alternate on the rungs and rest on top of them, not through them; the ladder stays against the wall.

caption: Two teammates run toward each other and high-five, their hands slapping together and stopping.
expectation: The hands stop at contact and rebound slightly; they do not pass through each other; each hand keeps five fingers.

caption: A baby crawls across a living-room rug toward a toy.
expectation: Hands and knees move in alternation, the body stays whole with two arms and two legs, and the baby moves forward only as the limbs move.

caption: A nurse folds a bedsheet in half lengthwise and then in half again, smoothing the folds flat.
expectation: The sheet bends along each fold and lies flat on itself; it gets smaller with each fold and does not stiffen or fold by itself.

caption: A man pulls a sock over his foot, stretching the opening and drawing the fabric up over his heel and ankle.
expectation: The sock stretches around the foot and follows its shape; the foot goes into the opening, not through the fabric.

caption: A florist wraps a bouquet in a sheet of cellophane, folding the sheet around the stems and creasing it at the corners.
expectation: The sheet bends around the stems and keeps the creases where pressed; it does not pass through the stems or unfold on its own.

caption: A deckhand throws a coil of rope onto the dock, and it lands in a loose tangle of loops.
expectation: The rope bends into loops that lie on top of one another; it does not pass through itself or land in a straight line.

caption: A boy pushes a coin under the edge of a rug with his finger, and when he lifts the rug the coin lies where he pushed it.
expectation: A small bump shows in the rug where the coin is; the coin is hidden while covered and is the same coin, in that spot, when the rug is lifted.

caption: A bus drives behind a tall building and emerges from the other side a moment later.
expectation: The bus is hidden for a time matching its speed and the building's width, and reappears at the same speed and heading; it does not show through the building.

caption: A boy drops a marble into the top of a long cardboard tube held upright, and the marble comes out of the bottom and rolls away.
expectation: The marble is hidden inside the tube and exits at the bottom after a short delay; the same marble comes out, and nothing exits before it enters.

caption: A cat crawls under a blanket on a bed, and a moving lump travels across the blanket to the far edge, where the cat comes out.
expectation: The lump is the cat's size and moves continuously; the cat is not visible through the blanket and emerges only at the edge.

caption: A slice of cheese is laid on a hot dog straight off the grill, and the cheese softens and slumps over the sides.
expectation: The slice loses its stiff edges and drapes down over the sausage; it does not stay square or re-harden on the hot surface.

caption: A child presses a warm cookie fresh from the oven, and the chocolate chips inside squash and smear under her finger.
expectation: The chips are soft and spread under pressure; they do not crack or stay hard while the cookie is warm.

caption: A woman drops an ice cube into a cup of hot tea, and the cube shrinks and disappears within moments.
expectation: The cube floats, rounds off, and gets smaller until it is gone; it does not grow or sink while still whole.

caption: A snowball thrown against a warm sunlit window sticks for a moment, then slides down the glass as it melts, leaving a wet streak.
expectation: The snow softens, slides downward, and leaves water behind; it does not climb or refreeze on the warm glass.

caption: A car's heater blows on a frost-covered side mirror, and the frost turns to droplets that run down the mirror.
expectation: The frost clears where the warm air reaches first and the water runs downward; the frost does not re-form while the heater runs.

caption: A lollipop left on a car dashboard in the sun sags and bends over on its stick.
expectation: The candy softens and droops downward under its own weight; it does not stand back up while warm.

caption: A cook dips an apple into hot caramel and sets it on a cold plate, and the caramel coating firms up into a glossy shell.
expectation: The caramel drips a little, slows, and stops running as it cools; the shell is firm and does not become liquid again.

caption: Melted chocolate from a fondue pot drips onto a chilled plate and sets into raised drops.
expectation: Each drop spreads slightly on landing, then stops and dulls as it sets; the drops do not keep flowing across the cold plate.

caption: A child's snow cone sits in the sun and melts into a puddle of coloured syrup in the paper cup.
expectation: The mound of ice shrinks and the liquid rises in the cup, keeping the colour; the ice does not re-form.

caption: A chocolate bunny left on a shelf beside a radiator slumps, and its ears droop and bend over.
expectation: The parts nearest the heat soften first and sag downward under their own weight; the bunny does not stand back up while warm.

caption: A cook stir-fries vegetables in a wok, and a cloud of steam rises with each toss.
expectation: Steam rises from the hot food and thins above the wok; each toss releases a fresh burst; it does not sink.

caption: A hot tub sits outside on a cold night, and steam drifts up from its surface into the dark.
expectation: The steam rises from the whole surface and drifts with any breeze, thinning as it rises; it does not settle downward.

caption: A woman runs a hot bath, and steam rises from the falling water and fills the bathroom.
expectation: The steam rises from the tap stream and the bath surface and collects near the ceiling; the mirror may fog.

caption: A man pours boiling water into a glass French press, and steam rises from the top while the coffee grounds swirl up through the water.
expectation: Steam rises from the open top and thins; the grounds churn up with the pour and settle afterwards; steam does not sink.

caption: A tenant opens the bleed valve on an old radiator, and a hiss of steam escapes until water spurts out and he shuts it.
expectation: The steam jet rises from the valve while it is open and stops when the water arrives and the valve is closed.

caption: A cleaner presses a steam cleaner nozzle to a carpet, and steam puffs out around the nozzle and the carpet darkens with damp.
expectation: Steam rises from around the nozzle only while the trigger is pressed and the carpet is wet where the nozzle has been.

caption: A pot of jam boils on a stove, and the surface foams up and bubbles thickly.
expectation: The foam rises while the heat is on and sinks back when the pot is pulled off; the bubbles burst slowly on the thick surface.

caption: A pot of potatoes boils with its lid on, and the lid rattles and lifts as steam escapes around its edge.
expectation: The lid jumps in time with the puffs of steam and steam rises from the gap; the rattling stops when the heat is turned down.

caption: A man pours hot water from a thermos onto a frozen car door lock, and steam rises from the lock as the ice runs off.
expectation: Steam rises where the hot water hits and the water runs downward off the door; the ice does not re-form while the water is hot.

caption: A barber unrolls a hot towel for a shave, and steam rises from the cloth as it opens.
expectation: Steam rises from the whole unfolded towel, thickest as it is first opened, and fades as the towel cools.

caption: A woman lifts cold cans of drink out of an ice bucket at a picnic, and the cans sweat and drip in the sun.
expectation: Moisture appears on the cans, gathers into drops, and runs down; the cans stay wet while cold.

caption: A snorkeler's mask fogs on the inside as she breathes while floating in warm water.
expectation: The fog forms on the inner surface and thickens with each breath; rinsing the mask clears it.

caption: A takeaway coffee cup with a plastic lid is set on a desk, and the underside of the lid clouds with droplets.
expectation: Droplets form on the inner face of the lid and drip back into the coffee; the outside of the lid stays dry.

caption: A chilled cocktail glass is set on a bar in a warm room, and a film of mist forms on it and turns into running drops.
expectation: The mist appears evenly on the cold glass and beads run down to wet the bar mat; the glass does not dry while cold.

caption: A metal water bottle packed with ice sits on a gym bench, and a wet patch spreads on the bench beneath it.
expectation: Droplets form on the cold metal and run down to the base, and the patch grows while the bottle stays cold.

caption: A shop worker opens the glass door of a walk-in freezer, and the door's glass fogs over as warm air hits it.
expectation: The fog forms on the cold glass within moments of opening and clears slowly once the door is shut and the glass warms.

caption: A cold yogurt tub taken from the fridge sits on a sunny windowsill, and the lid and sides bead with water.
expectation: Moisture appears on the cold plastic and forms drops that run down; the tub does not dry off while cold.

caption: A man exhales onto his cold sunglasses to clean them, and the lenses fog and then clear as he wipes.
expectation: The fog appears with the breath and vanishes where the cloth passes; the wiped part stays clear.

caption: A dentist puts a small cold mirror into a patient's mouth, and the mirror fogs over at once; she wipes it and it clears.
expectation: The fog appears the moment the cold mirror meets the warm breath and clears where wiped; it re-fogs if left in.

caption: A cyclist stops at a light on a frosty morning, and his glasses fog with his heavy breathing; they clear again as he rides on.
expectation: The lenses cloud while he breathes hard standing still and clear once moving air passes over them.

caption: A man opens the door of a wood stove, and the flames inside lean out toward the opening and flare up.
expectation: The flames grow and lean as the door opens and settle back when it shuts; they always point upward from the logs.

caption: A birthday cake with lit candles is carried across a room, and the flames lean backward as it moves and stand up when it is set down.
expectation: The flames trail opposite to the direction of motion, flicker, and return to pointing upward when the cake stops; none goes out unless blown.

caption: A farmer burns stubble in a field, and a line of flame advances across the field with the wind, smoke drifting ahead of it.
expectation: The fire line moves downwind, blackened ground is left behind it, and the smoke leans the same way as the flames.

caption: A man uses a small blowtorch to light charcoal in a barbecue, and the coals begin to glow where the flame touches them.
expectation: The glow appears only where the torch is aimed and spreads slowly to neighbouring coals; the flame points where the torch points.

caption: A boy tosses a dry pine cone into a fireplace, and it catches, glows, and crumbles into embers.
expectation: The cone lights where it touches the flames, burns from that side, and shrinks into glowing pieces that fade; it does not return whole.

caption: A candle burns inside a glass lantern hung outdoors, and its flame flickers as gusts pass but stays lit.
expectation: The flame leans and dances with each gust and stands upright between gusts; the glass protects it from going out.

caption: A man drops a lit match into a puddle, and it goes out with a tiny hiss and floats dark on the water.
expectation: The flame dies the instant the match hits the water and does not relight; a wisp of smoke rises.

caption: Bread left too long in a toaster smokes, and a grey plume rises from the slots.
expectation: The smoke rises straight up from the slots and spreads near the ceiling; it does not pour out sideways along the counter.

caption: A cook fans the glowing coals of a grill with a piece of cardboard, and the coals brighten with each wave.
expectation: The glow intensifies during each wave and eases between them; sparks may lift with the air and fade.

caption: A child pokes a campfire with a stick until its tip catches fire, then pulls it out and blows it out, leaving a glowing ember that slowly fades.
expectation: The tip lights only while in the flames, the flame dies at the puff of breath, and the ember dims steadily; it does not reflame on its own.

caption: A sealed yogurt pot left in a hot car bulges until its foil lid domes upward.
expectation: The lid rises gradually as the car heats and stays domed in the heat; it does not sink inward.

caption: A hot-air popcorn machine is switched on, and popped kernels burst out of the chute into a bowl.
expectation: Kernels pop into much larger pieces and are blown out only after the machine has heated; the flow stops when it is switched off.

caption: A camper's inflatable pillow left in a tent under the midday sun swells until it is taut and firm.
expectation: The pillow grows firmer and rounder as the tent heats and softens again in the evening; it does not shrink in the heat.

caption: Candles are lit beneath a wooden Christmas pyramid, and its fan blades start turning and the figures rotate.
expectation: The blades turn only after the candles are lit and slow to a stop when they are blown out.

caption: Heat shimmer rises off the black roof of a car parked in the sun, and the building behind the car wavers through it.
expectation: The shimmer rises from the hot roof and fades with height; the building itself does not move.

caption: A hot dog on a grill sizzles, and its skin splits open along its length with a pop.
expectation: The split appears suddenly along one line and gapes open; it does not close again.

caption: A cook drops a papadum into hot oil, and it puffs up and doubles in size within seconds.
expectation: The flat disc blisters and expands as soon as it hits the oil and keeps its puffed shape when lifted out; it does not shrink back.

caption: A cook sets a pan straight from the stove onto a thin plastic cutting board, and the board warps and its edges lift.
expectation: The board bends under and around the hot pan and keeps some of the warp after the pan is removed; it does not stay perfectly flat.

caption: A sealed bag of chips left on a hot dashboard puffs up tight like a pillow.
expectation: The bag swells gradually in the heat and stays swollen; it does not shrink in the hot car.

caption: A cook slides rice crackers into hot oil, and they swell and float to the surface.
expectation: The crackers puff up within moments of entering the oil and rise to float; they do not sink once puffed or shrink back.

caption: A street performer juggles three balls in the afternoon sun, and the shadows of the balls dance across the pavement beneath him.
expectation: Each ball has one shadow that moves with it on the ground, offset away from the sun; the shadows meet the balls only when they are caught low.

caption: A woman walks her dog past a floodlit sports field at night, and their shadows stretch long across the grass away from the lights.
expectation: Both shadows lie on the side away from the floodlights, move with the walkers, and stay attached at their feet.

caption: A child holds a toy plane up in the sun and swoops it around, and the plane's shadow swoops across the sandpit below.
expectation: The shadow moves in step with the toy, grows larger as the toy is lowered toward the sand, and lies away from the sun.

caption: A cook holds a whisk between a lamp and a kitchen wall, and the shadow of the whisk's wires appears on the wall and spins as she twirls it.
expectation: The shadow shows the wire outline, turns as the whisk turns, and disappears when she moves the whisk out of the light.

caption: A parked bicycle casts a sharp shadow on a sunny wall, and a passing cloud makes the shadow fade and then return.
expectation: The shadow softens and vanishes as the cloud covers the sun and comes back in the same place when the sun returns; the bike does not move.

caption: A tennis player serves at night under stadium floodlights, and several faint shadows fan out from her feet in different directions.
expectation: Each shadow points away from one of the floodlights; they all move with her and none points toward a light.

caption: A hiker holds a map up in bright sun, and the shadow of the map falls across her body and the ground.
expectation: The shadow has the map's rectangular outline, lies on the side away from the sun, and moves when the map moves.

caption: A cat sits on a sunny fence, jumps down, and its shadow leaves the fence and lands with it on the ground.
expectation: The shadow stays on the surfaces below the cat, separates during the jump, and rejoins at the paws on landing.

caption: A stage technician moves a spotlight across a dancer, and the dancer's shadow on the backdrop swings the opposite way.
expectation: The shadow moves in the direction opposite to the light's movement and always falls away from the spotlight.

caption: A jogger runs across a bridge at sunset, and her long shadow runs along the bridge deck beside her.
expectation: The shadow is much longer than she is tall, lies on the side away from the low sun, and keeps pace with her.

caption: A woman applies lipstick using the reflection in a car's side mirror, and the reflected hand moves the lipstick in step with hers.
expectation: The reflection moves at the same instant and is mirrored; it shows her face at the size the small mirror allows.

caption: A family stands on a jetty over a still lake, and their upside-down reflections stand beneath them in the water.
expectation: The reflections are inverted, joined at the jetty's waterline, and move with the people; they blur where a ripple passes.

caption: A child sticks her tongue out at a shop window, and her reflection in the glass sticks its tongue out back.
expectation: The reflected face moves at the same instant and is faint over the goods displayed behind the glass; it is mirrored.

caption: A boy wipes a fogged bus window with his sleeve at night, and his reflection appears in the clear patch.
expectation: The reflection appears only in the wiped patch and moves with him; the fogged parts stay blurred.

caption: A child looks into a puddle as a bird flies overhead, and the bird's reflection crosses the puddle upside down and leaves at its edge.
expectation: The reflected bird appears only within the puddle, inverted, and moves in step with the real bird.

caption: A woman swings a wardrobe's mirrored door closed, and the reflected room sweeps across the mirror until it shows only the wall.
expectation: The scene in the mirror slides smoothly as the door turns and changes to whatever the mirror faces; it does not stay fixed on one view.

caption: A man adjusts a mirror in a hallway so that the front door appears in it, and the door's reflection shifts as he tilts the mirror.
expectation: The reflected door slides across the mirror as it tilts and leaves the mirror when the angle is too great.

caption: A dog drinks from a still pond, and its reflection breaks into ripples where its tongue touches the water.
expectation: The reflection is inverted and sharp until the tongue touches; it fragments where ripples spread and settles when the dog stops.

caption: A car drives past a puddle at night, and the reflections of its headlights slide across the puddle's surface.
expectation: The reflected lights move with the car and appear only within the puddle's edges; they vanish when the car has passed.

caption: A woman polishes a brass doorknob until her face appears in it, small and warped.
expectation: The reflection appears as the surface is polished, is curved by the knob, and moves when she moves.

caption: A boy stands a pencil in a glass of water, and the pencil appears to break at the waterline.
expectation: The apparent break is at the surface and vanishes when the pencil is lifted out; the pencil itself is straight.

caption: A woman peers through the glass door of an oven at a cake inside, and the cake is visible until the glass steams over and hides it.
expectation: The cake is seen clearly through the clear glass and becomes a blur as the fog forms from the inside; wiping the outside does not clear it.

caption: A man reads a menu through the clear glass top of a café table, and the menu is legible through the glass.
expectation: The menu is seen sharply through the glass with a faint reflection over it; the glass does not hide it.

caption: A child watches a goldfish through a curved bowl, and the fish appears to swell and shrink as it swims around the curve.
expectation: The size change happens only through the curved glass and water; the fish keeps its true size and shape.

caption: A woman holds a magnifying glass over a map, and the streets under the lens appear enlarged and shift as she moves it.
expectation: Only the area under the lens is enlarged and it moves with the lens; the map outside is normal.

caption: A cat sits behind a glass patio door watching a bird on the lawn, paws at the glass, and cannot reach the bird.
expectation: The bird is visible through the glass and the paw stops at the pane; the cat does not pass through and the bird is not hidden.

caption: A boy looks at a lamp through a clear glass bottle of water, and the lamp appears stretched and doubled through the bottle.
expectation: The distortion is confined to the view through the water and changes as the bottle turns; the lamp itself is unchanged.

caption: A child looks at the street lights through a glass of fizzy water, and the lights wobble and sparkle as bubbles rise through the glass.
expectation: The distortion changes with the rising bubbles and the lights are steady when seen past the glass; the lights themselves do not move.

caption: A motorcyclist's visor is speckled with rain, and the road lights ahead smear into streaks until he wipes the visor with his glove.
expectation: The smearing follows the drops and clears where the glove passes; the lights are sharp through the wiped area.

caption: A child looks at a flower through a clear glass paperweight, and the flower appears bloated and curved through the glass.
expectation: The distortion appears only through the glass and moves as the paperweight moves; the flower is normal beside it.

caption: A woman enters a dark garage and pulls the cord of a bare bulb, and the garage is lit.
expectation: The room goes from dark to lit at the pull and stays lit; sharp shadows of the tools appear away from the bulb.

caption: A camper points a headlamp at a tent wall and turns his head slowly, and the bright patch slides across the canvas.
expectation: The patch moves with his head and the canvas he looks away from darkens; the light is brightest at the patch's centre.

caption: A man lights a lantern in a dark barn, and the nearby hay and beams brighten while the far end stays in shadow.
expectation: Brightness is greatest near the lantern and falls off with distance; shadows fall away from it.

caption: A woman turns off a floor lamp in a living room, and the corner of the room goes dark while the rest stays lit by the ceiling light.
expectation: Only the lamp's light disappears; the corner it lit darkens while other areas are unchanged.

caption: A car with its headlights on turns a corner at night, and the beams sweep across a row of parked cars.
expectation: Each parked car brightens as the beams cross it and darkens after; the lit area moves with the turning car.

caption: A boy holds a flashlight against his palm in a dark room, and his fingers glow red at the edges.
expectation: The glow appears only where the flesh is thin and disappears when the light is turned off; little light passes through the palm.

caption: A projector is switched on in a dark classroom, and the screen lights up while the faces in the front row glow in its light.
expectation: The screen is bright and the nearby faces are lit from the screen's direction; the back of the room stays dim.

caption: A woman opens a laptop in a dark bedroom, and the screen's glow lights her face and the pillow beside her.
expectation: The glow appears when the screen lights, is strongest on surfaces facing it, and changes with the picture.

caption: A watchman walks along a dark corridor with a torch, and the doors ahead are lit one by one as he approaches and darken behind him.
expectation: The lit area travels with the torch; doors brighten as the beam reaches them and darken once it has passed.

caption: The sun comes out from behind a cloud over a beach, and the sand and sea brighten all at once.
expectation: The whole scene brightens together and sharp shadows appear; it dims again when the next cloud passes.

caption: A child kneads a lump of red play-dough together with a lump of blue, and the mixture turns purple.
expectation: Purple appears where the two colours fold together and spreads until no streaks remain; the colours do not separate again.

caption: A child drops a blue bath tablet into a bathtub, and blue spreads through the water until it is evenly tinted.
expectation: The colour spreads from the tablet in plumes and evens out; the water does not become clear again.

caption: A green spotlight is aimed at a white marble statue in a garden at night, and the statue appears green.
expectation: The statue takes the light's colour only where the beam falls and returns to white when the light is switched off.

caption: Afternoon sun shines through a stained-glass lampshade on a windowsill, and coloured patches of light appear on the ceiling above it.
expectation: Each patch matches the colour of the glass it came through and lies on the side away from the sun; the patches fade when the sun is covered.

caption: A rainbow appears in the mist at the foot of a waterfall on a sunny day, and fades when a cloud covers the sun.
expectation: The rainbow sits within the mist opposite the sun, keeps its arc while the sun shines, and disappears when the sun is hidden.

caption: A cook stirs a spoonful of cocoa into a glass of white milk, and the milk turns brown.
expectation: Brown swirls spread from the spoon and even out; the milk does not return to white.

caption: A cyclist in a white jacket rides under an orange streetlamp and the jacket looks amber, then looks white again under a white LED lamp further on.
expectation: The jacket's colour follows the light falling on it and changes as she passes from one lamp to the next.

caption: A child holds a piece of green glass up to the sky, and the clouds seen through it look green.
expectation: Only the view through the glass is tinted; the sky around it is unchanged.

caption: A crystal vase on a sunny table throws small rainbow flecks onto the wall, and they move as someone bumps the table.
expectation: The flecks appear only while the sun hits the vase, shift when the vase moves, and vanish when a cloud covers the sun.

caption: A bartender pours blue liqueur into a glass of orange juice and stirs, and the drink turns a murky green-brown.
expectation: The colour changes where the liquids meet and evens out with stirring; the layers do not separate back.

caption: A janitor flips a bank of switches in a school gym, and rows of ceiling lights come on one bank at a time.
expectation: Each row lights at its own switch and only then; rows whose switch is untouched stay dark.

caption: A woman turns the key on a desk lamp's base, and the lamp lights; she turns it again and it goes dark.
expectation: The light changes state exactly at each click and never on its own.

caption: A man presses the button on a bicycle's front light, and it starts to flash; he holds the button and it switches to a steady beam.
expectation: The light responds only to the presses, flashing then steady; it does not change mode by itself.

caption: A woman taps the touch panel of an induction hob, and the ring's indicator light comes on and the pan begins to warm.
expectation: The indicator lights at the tap; nothing lights before; tapping off darkens it.

caption: A boy pulls the trigger of a battery-powered toy gun, and its barrel lights up and its motor whirs.
expectation: The light and whir start at the trigger pull and stop when it is released.

caption: A shopkeeper presses the switch on a rotating display stand, and the stand begins to turn with its lights on.
expectation: The stand turns and lights only after the switch; it stops and darkens when switched off.

caption: A man switches on a bathroom extractor fan with the light switch, and the fan blades spin up as the light comes on.
expectation: The fan starts with the light and stops a while after it is switched off; it does not spin with the switch off.

caption: A child presses the big red button on a toy fire engine, and its roof lights flash.
expectation: The flashing starts at the press and stops after a set time or another press; the lights are dark before.

caption: A woman flips the switch for a porch light at dusk, and the porch is lit while the garden beyond stays dark.
expectation: The light comes on at the switch, lights the porch, and goes off at the switch; nothing else changes.

caption: A man unplugs a running desk fan, and the blades slow and stop.
expectation: The blades coast to a stop within a couple of seconds of the plug coming out even though the switch is still on.

caption: A child inserts batteries into a toy keyboard and presses a key, and the key lights and the speaker cone twitches.
expectation: The toy works only after the batteries are in; before that pressing keys does nothing.

caption: A woman plugs in a slow cooker and turns its dial to high, and the indicator light comes on; she unplugs it and the light goes out.
expectation: The light comes on only once plugged in and switched on, and goes off the instant the plug is pulled.

caption: A man's electric shaver dies mid-shave as its battery runs out, and it will not restart when he presses the button.
expectation: The buzzing stops and stays stopped despite presses; it works again only after charging.

caption: A power cut hits a restaurant, and every light and the neon sign in the window go dark at once while the candles on the tables keep burning.
expectation: All electric lights fail at the same instant; the candle flames are unaffected.

caption: A worker connects a floodlight to a running generator, and the floodlight comes on.
expectation: The lamp lights once plugged into the running generator and goes out if the generator is stopped.

caption: A child's remote-control boat slows and stops in the middle of a pond as its battery runs flat.
expectation: The boat loses speed gradually and drifts to a stop; the controller no longer moves it.

caption: A man drops a wireless earbud into its charging case, and a small light on the case begins to blink.
expectation: The light starts only when the earbud is seated in the case and stops when it is taken out.

caption: A runner on a treadmill pulls out the safety key, and the belt slows and stops; it starts again only when the key is reinserted.
expectation: The belt coasts to a stop within a second or two of the key coming out and does not move until the key is back and the start pressed.

caption: Lightning flashes over a vineyard at night, and the rows of vines are lit for an instant before the dark returns.
expectation: The flash is brief and lights everything at once; the vines are dark again immediately.

caption: A lightning bolt strikes a hilltop radio mast, and the mast is outlined in a bright flash.
expectation: The bolt ends at the mast's tip, the flash lasts a fraction of a second, and the mast stands unchanged afterwards.

caption: A family watches a storm from a covered porch, and a flash lights their faces before they flinch at the thunder.
expectation: The flash comes first and the reaction after; the light is gone before the reaction.

caption: Lightning flashes over a snowy village at night, and the snow-covered roofs and street flash white for an instant.
expectation: The whole scene brightens together for a fraction of a second and returns to dark; the house lights stay steady.

caption: A bolt of lightning forks from a cloud to a lone barn in a field, and smoke rises from the barn roof after the flash.
expectation: The bolt is brief and ends at the barn; the smoke appears after and rises; the roof does not glow.

caption: Lightning flickers inside a thunderhead over a desert highway, lighting the cloud from within again and again.
expectation: Each flicker is brief and lights the cloud, not the ground directly; no bolt reaches the road.

caption: A lightning flash lights a hospital room through the blinds, throwing the blinds' striped shadow across the bed for an instant.
expectation: The stripes appear on the side away from the window only during the flash and vanish with it.

caption: Lightning strikes the sea near a fishing boat at night, and the water around the strike is lit for an instant.
expectation: The bolt comes down to the water, the flash reflects on the surface, and darkness returns at once.

caption: A rescue crew cuts a car roof with a power saw, and sparks spray from the blade across the wet road.
expectation: Sparks fly out along the blade's direction, arc down onto the road, and die; they appear only while the blade is cutting.

caption: A mechanic grinds a rusty bolt with a bench grinder, and a fan of sparks shoots off the wheel toward the floor.
expectation: The sparks leave tangent to the wheel, arc down, and fade; they stop when the bolt is lifted away.

caption: A skier's metal ski edges scrape across an exposed rock, and sparks flash from under the skis.
expectation: The sparks appear only during the scrape and go dark instantly; none appear on snow.

caption: A trolleybus turns a corner on a wet evening, and its poles flash sparks against the overhead wires.
expectation: The sparks appear at the contact points and move with the bus; each flash is brief and no burning drops fall.

caption: A hiker strikes a flint and steel over a pile of dry grass, and sparks fall onto the grass and one catches into a glow.
expectation: The sparks fall downward and most die in the air; the glow appears where a spark landed, after the strike.

caption: A car's exhaust pipe scrapes a speed bump at night, and a brief spray of sparks shoots out behind the car.
expectation: The sparks appear only during the scrape, trail backward, and fade at once.

caption: A mechanic accidentally lays a wrench across both terminals of a car battery, and it sparks and jumps.
expectation: The spark flashes at the moment of contact and the wrench twitches; the spark is gone as soon as contact breaks.

caption: A neon sign's box shorts in the rain, and sparks drop from beneath the sign onto the wet pavement.
expectation: The sparks fall downward from the sign box and go dark before or as they land; the sign flickers with each spark.

caption: A child sticks a magnet to a steel locker door, and it holds a drawing in place.
expectation: The magnet stays on the vertical steel with the paper under it and does not slide down.

caption: A mechanic drops a screw into a narrow gap and fishes it out with a magnet on a stick, the screw jumping to the magnet.
expectation: The screw leaps only when the magnet is close and hangs from it as it is lifted out.

caption: A teacher slides a magnet under a sheet of card, and a steel ball on top of the card rolls to follow it.
expectation: The ball moves only where the magnet moves beneath and stays on top of the card; it stops when the magnet stops.

caption: A woman drops a steel spoon toward a knife rack's magnetic strip, and the spoon swerves and clicks onto the strip.
expectation: The spoon's fall bends toward the strip only when close and it stops dead on contact.

caption: A boy holds two toy train cars end to end and turns one around, and the ends that repelled now snap together.
expectation: With one orientation the cars push apart; after turning one, they pull together over the last gap and stay joined.

caption: A teacher tosses a whiteboard eraser with a magnetic back at the whiteboard, and it sticks where it hits.
expectation: The eraser stops dead on contact and stays on the vertical board; it does not bounce off or slide down.

caption: A child sweeps a magnet through a sandbox and lifts it out coated in dark grains while the sand falls away.
expectation: Only the dark iron grains cling to the magnet; the ordinary sand drops back into the box.

caption: A shopper sticks a magnetic phone holder to a steel shelf and hangs a phone on it, and both hold.
expectation: The holder stays on the vertical steel with the phone's weight and does not slide.

caption: A child pulls two plastic cups apart from a stack, and one cup clings to her fingers and has to be shaken off.
expectation: The cup stays on her hand when she opens her fingers and drops only after a shake; the other cups in the stack stay put.

caption: A woman pulls a fleece hat off a toddler, and the toddler's fine hair stands straight up.
expectation: The hair rises as the hat comes off and settles slowly; it is flat before the hat moves.

caption: A man unloads laundry from a dryer, and a dryer sheet clings to the back of his shirt without his noticing.
expectation: The sheet stays stuck to the fabric as he moves and does not fall until pulled off.

caption: A girl slides down a plastic slide and reaches for the metal ladder at the bottom, and she jerks her hand back at the shock.
expectation: The jerk happens at the moment of contact with the metal, not before.

caption: A man peels the protective film off a new television screen, and the film clings to his arm and crackles.
expectation: The film sticks to skin and to itself where it touches and has to be pulled free; it does not drop straight down.

caption: A boy rubs a plastic pen on his sleeve and holds it over a scattering of pepper on a plate, and the pepper grains jump onto the pen.
expectation: Grains leap only when the rubbed pen is close and cling to it; an unrubbed pen does nothing.

caption: A cat rubs against a wool blanket in a dark room, and tiny sparks crackle in its fur.
expectation: The sparks appear only where the fur moves against the wool and vanish instantly; nothing glows when the cat is still.

caption: A woman rubs a balloon on her sleeve and holds it near a length of curling ribbon hanging from a gift, and the ribbon leans toward the balloon.
expectation: The ribbon swings toward the balloon only when it is close and hangs straight again when it is moved away.

caption: A child strikes a large temple bell with a wooden beam, and the bell's rim shimmers and the bell sways on its hanger.
expectation: The shimmer and sway begin at the strike and die away over several seconds; the bell is still before.

caption: A boy strikes a horseshoe hanging from a string with a nail, and the horseshoe rings and quivers on its string.
expectation: The quiver and swing begin at the strike and fade over a few seconds; the horseshoe is still before.

caption: A cook bangs a wok with a ladle, and the wok rings and quivers on its stand.
expectation: The quiver starts at the bang and fades within a second or two.

caption: A gymnast dismounts from a balance beam, and the beam shivers along its length before settling.
expectation: The shiver starts as she pushes off and dies away quickly; the beam is still before and after.

caption: A man flicks the blade of a handsaw held by its handle, and the blade wobbles in a blur before going still.
expectation: The blur is widest at the tip right after the flick and shrinks to stillness; the handle stays sharp.

caption: A drummer hits a hanging tom-tom, and the head dips and shivers before returning flat.
expectation: The first dip is deepest and the rebounds shrink; the head is flat within a couple of seconds.

caption: A child kicks a chain-link fence, and the mesh shivers outward from the kick along the panel.
expectation: The shiver spreads from the kick point and dies away within seconds; the fence is still before.

caption: A bass guitarist plays a low note through an amplifier, and the water in a glass on the amp shivers into ripples.
expectation: The ripples appear with the note and vanish when it stops; the glass does not slide off.

caption: A garbage truck idles outside a house, and a hanging wind chime by the door trembles and tinkles while the engine runs.
expectation: The trembling lasts while the truck idles and stops after it drives away; the chime is still in quiet air.

caption: A door is slammed in a hallway, and a framed mirror on the adjacent wall rocks on its hook before hanging still.
expectation: The rocking begins at the slam and dies out over a few seconds; the mirror does not move before.

caption: A brass band plays in a square, and the loose glass of a nearby café window buzzes with the tuba notes.
expectation: The buzzing appears on the low notes and stops between them; the window is still when the band stops.

caption: A cement mixer rumbles beside a garden wall, and pebbles on the wall's top shiver and shift.
expectation: The pebbles move only while the mixer runs and settle when it stops.

caption: A church organ plays a deep pedal note, and a hymn book on a nearby pew shivers and slides to the edge.
expectation: The book moves only while the low note sounds and stops when it ends.

caption: A heavy freight train passes a level crossing, and the coins in a cup holder of a waiting car rattle.
expectation: The rattling starts as the train arrives, is strongest as it passes, and stops once it has gone.

caption: A moped idles at a kerb, and its exhaust pipe quivers visibly until the engine is switched off.
expectation: The quiver lasts as long as the engine runs and stops within a moment of it being cut.

caption: A phone on vibrate buzzes on a nightstand and works its way to the edge before the alarm is silenced.
expectation: The phone moves in small jerks only while buzzing and stops the moment it is silenced.

caption: A violinist plays a fast passage, and the bowed strings blur under the bow and sharpen as the bow lifts.
expectation: Only the strings under the moving bow blur; they are sharp when the bow is off them.

caption: A cook runs a hand-held blender in a jug of soup, and the shaft blurs and the jug trembles until she releases the button.
expectation: The blur and trembling exist only while the button is held and stop when it is released.

caption: A carillon bell in a tower is struck by its hammer, and the hammer swings back while the bell's rim quivers.
expectation: The hammer moves only to strike and retreat; the quiver begins at the strike and fades.

caption: A jackhammer is started on a pavement, and its bit blurs and the whole tool shudders in the worker's hands until he releases the trigger.
expectation: The shuddering lasts as long as the trigger is held and stops when it is released.
